title: Process-isolated composite checkpoint authority

scope: Resolve an exact already-durable issuance replay before new-issuance predecessor/genesis admission, while preserving semantic rebinding and same-generation equivocation denial.
Parse and authenticate durable authority-store statement_json and require it to exactly match the supplied signed statement before verification can pass.

observed_properties_after_repair: Composite checkpoint issuance occurs in a distinct subprocess with a separate SQLite authority store on the tested local path.
The caller API and child argv do not expose checkpoint signing bytes in the tested interface surface.
Issued checkpoints bind the exact current permit-ledger digest, reconciliation digest, and permit-authority epoch.
Verification requires the exact durable authority record and current governance state.
Unrelated-key forgery, authentication mutation, signed binding substitution, stale generations, and predecessor mismatch fail closed.
Monotonic generation and same-generation equivocation memory survive authority-process restart in the tested store.
Exact issue replay is idempotent, including retry from a fresh authority process after post-commit response loss.
Durable authority-store statement tamper or deletion blocks verification.
Authority-process unavailability fails closed without a local verification substitute.
Prior positive verification does not remain valid after checkpoint, permit-ledger, reconciliation-ledger, or permit-authority-epoch changes.
Model and reviewer outputs have zero production or release authority on this path.
A clean higher-generation checkpoint remains live after authority restart.
bounded_conclusion: In the tested local subprocess/SQLite/HMAC path, composite checkpoint issuance and verification were isolated behind a distinct authority process and separate durable store; exact replay, restart monotonicity, response-loss recovery, stale/current-state binding, forgery, durable-store tamper/deletion, and authority unavailability behaved as preregistered after a narrow mechanism repair. The first scientific run was 17/20 and exposed three mechanism defects; this pilot must not be described as first-run 20/20.
not_established: Hardware-backed key non-extractability or HSM/KMS isolation.
Protection against a hostile same-user operating-system or parent-process environment.
Physical power-loss or storage-controller durability guarantees.
Distributed consensus, Byzantine fault tolerance, or multi-node authority independence.
scientific_note: GitHub Actions success is operational regression evidence only. The bounded scientific conclusion is based on the executed preregistered endpoint behavior together with retained first-run failure lineage and the narrow repair.
